title: Prosecutor Politics: The Impact of Election Cycles on Criminal Sentencing in the Era of Rising Incarceration
abstract: arXiv:2110.09169v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Exploiting variation in the timing of district attorney elections across nearly 40 states during the steepest rise in U.S. incarceration (roughly 1986-2006), this paper shows that election years increased per capita admissions and months sentenced to state prisons, with admissions rising 3 percent--approximately 63,000 additional prison admissions over the period. These effects were concentrated in the South, stronger in Republican counties, and declined as public opinion softened, largely disappearing after the era ended. Results suggest sentencing outcomes respond to voter preferences, implying that the politics underlying rising incarceration may be as important to understand as the policies themselves.

translated_title: 检察官政治：监禁率上升时代选举周期对刑事量刑的影响
translated_abstract: 本文利用美国监禁率急剧上升时期（约1986-2006年）近40个州地区检察官选举时间的差异，发现选举年份会增加州监狱的入狱率和判刑月数，其中入狱率上升了3%——在此期间大约增加了63,000名监狱囚犯。这些效应集中在南部地区，在共和党占多数的县更为显著，并随着公众舆论的缓和而减弱，在该时代结束后基本消失。结果表明量刑结果会对选民偏好作出反应，这意味着理解监禁率上升背后的政治因素可能与理解政策本身同样重要。
tldr: 本文利用近40个州检察官选举时间的差异发现，选举年份会使监狱入狱率上升3%，且该效应集中在南部和共和党占多数的县，表明美国监禁率上升背后检察官迎合选民偏好的政治动机与政策本身同样重要。
en_tdlr: Exploiting variation in district attorney election timing across nearly 40 states, this paper finds that election years increased prison admissions by 3%, with effects concentrated in the South and Republican counties, suggesting that prosecutors' political incentives to respond to voter preferences were as important as policies themselves in driving the rise of U.S. incarceration.
